title: Pacing and pin concurrency playbook (personal notes)
content:
Context and intent:
- Personal scratchpad for a phased roll (canary -> ramp -> pin -> unpin) when flipping model versions or quantization variants.
- Focus: pacing (how much traffic over time), per-tenant concurrency caps, and safe unpin strategy that avoids cold-start avalanches.
- Not a formal runbook but intended to be read by SRE/serving engineers doing the flip.

Key constraints we need to respect:
- Latency SLO p95 < 250ms for standard tier, p99 < 600ms (on Dedicated).
- Error budget strictness during business hours: 0.01% error rate allowed, otherwise freeze ramp.
- KV cache warming is slow for large context tenants. Avoid big client cohorts flipping simultaneously.

High-level plan (phasewise):
1) Canary (0.5% traffic global) — 30 minutes observation window
   - Targets: telemetry p50/p95/p99, token error rate (400/500), model-qa regression (score on 50 prompt eval set), crash-free metric.
   - Concurrency cap: 2 per-tenant on canary variant.
   - Warmup: pre-warm by replaying recent 500 requests (synthetic) for top 10 tenants (CS to approve).
   - Slack alert template: see bottom.

2) Mini-ramp (2% -> 10% over 3 hours)
   - Step increases every 30 minutes, pause for 20min observation between steps.
   - Increase tenant concurrency caps gradually: 2 -> 4 -> 8.
   - Watch for tail latency and KV miss spikes. If KV miss > 15% (baseline 3%), rollback to previous fraction.

3) Anchor / Pin (25% cohort anchoring + reserved-pin for select customers)
   - Allocate pinned slots for paying customers that require stability. Pin map: preserve current model for those customers for 48 hours, then consider unpin test.
   - Use routing tag: routing.pin=customer-id to maintain affinity.

4) Full roll (if metrics stable)
   - Gradually expand to 100% over 2 days. Keep automatic fallback policy enabled (fallback to quantized variant if memory pressure or OOM).

Per-tenant concurrency & safe caps notes:
- Default conservative cap = max(2, floor(avg-qps * 0.2)) during canary window.
- For tenants with large sequence lengths (> 2k tokens median), cap at 1 or schedule later.
- For tenants with async SDKs: validate their retry/backoff behavior before increasing concurrency.

Telemetry thresholds and gating signals (fast checks):
- Latency: p95 increase > 25% relative to baseline -> pause.
- Errors: 5xx spikes (5x baseline) sustained 3min -> rollback.
- Quality: automated eval loss increase > 0.8% on golden prompts -> hold.
- User-facing regressions: CS reports >2 escalations in 1 hour -> freeze.
- Resource: GPU memory tilt (OOM events) -> immediate variant fallback.

KV cache warmup & priming strategy:
- Warmup synthetic generator (replay service): pick N recent requests per tenant up to 1k and push to canary pool with low QPS to populate KV cache.
- For models with quantization changes: run a small sampled warmup (50 requests x top 5 tenants) because quantized KV layout might differ and cause perf anomalies.

Soft-unpin (how to unpin safely):
- Do not unpin more than 10% of pinned tenants in any 24h window.
- For each unpin candidate: run a shadow comparison for 2 hours (route 1% to new variant under independent observability).
- If warmup fails (p95 increases) re-pin and flag for manual analysis.

Emergency rollback commands (ops cheat):
- Immediate rollback (global): /infra roll model-set --to previous --force (requires duty auth)
- Per-region rollback: /infra roll region us-west --to previous
- Per-tenant pining: /routing set-pin --tenant <id> --model <sha>
- Quick throttle: /traffic throttle --to 20% --reason "safety"
(These are shorthand; check internal infra CLI for exact syntax.)

Canary experiments and hypothesis to validate during canary:
- Hypothesis A: Quantized variant gives 1.7x token throughput without regressing top-10 prompt accuracy more than 1%. Test: run 1k golden prompts, compare logits/top1.
- Hypothesis B: Batching improvements reduce p95 for small requests (<64 tokens). Test: heat small-request cohort and measure per-token latency.

Checklist: Pre-deploy (must check)
- [ ] CI green: runtime tests and model validation PR merged (linked).
- [ ] Smoke image built and pushed to staging registry.
- [ ] Warmup synthetic sets prepared for top N tenants (CS list).
- [ ] Canary launch window scheduled on calendar with SRE and on-call.
- [ ] Slack channel #deploy-<id> created with notification hooks.
- [ ] Observability alerts staged (latency/error/kv-miss).
- [ ] Backout PR ready (fast revert).

Checklist: During canary
- [ ] Confirm canary traffic routed.
- [ ] Monitor telemetry every 5 minutes first 30 min, then 15 minutes.
- [ ] Post to #deploy-<id> every check-window with snapshot (p50/p95, 5xx count, KV miss, eval-score).
- [ ] CS on-call informed for pinned customers.

Post-mortem triggers (auto):
- Any rollback within 24h -> write short postmortem (what, when, impact, fix).
- If quality regression on golden set -> schedule evaluation triage with model owner.

Slack alert template (copy/paste):
- "[ALERT] Canary flip: model vX.Y -> vX.Y+1 started. Window: 30m. Initial fraction: 0.5%. Watch p95/p99 + 5xx. Link: <deployment_link>. On-call: @oncall-sre. If issues react: /infra roll --to previous."

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How to encode per-tenant warmup priority in routing layer? (ticket?)
- Need a safety metric for hallucinations — can we auto-check hallucination risk with a small NLI classifier on golden set?
- Should we expose a client-facing SDK toggle for delayed model swap (client opt-in)? Pros/cons.

Random scraps / heuristics I keep thinking about:
- Stagger by QPS buckets rather than tenant alphabetical to avoid correlated warmups.
- Prefer evening quiet-windows for non-critical tenants, midday for enterprise tenants with SRE standing by.
- Keep a rolling list of 10 tenants to never unpin without explicit CS signoff (billing impact).

If you touch this doc: leave date and short note at top.

-- Luke
